meta.title: Bear hunt — Kingshot 777
meta.description: TL;DR guide to the Kingshot Bear Hunt event: rally formations, troop ratios, buffs, and wave timing.

tldr.heading: TL;DR
items: Archers win. Bear damage scales with archers — ratios shift from balanced in Gen 1 to 10/10/80 by Gen 4, and up to ~98% archers late game.
Rally leader: all three heroes' skills are active, so pick the best offensive trio for your generation.
Joining a rally: only the top expedition skill of the top 4 joiners with max skill counts. Wrong hero hurts the rally — send troops with no hero instead.
Always on: pet buff + Field Commander minister buff. Gems for city ATK / Lethality / Deployment if you can afford it.
Be fast: pre-save preset formations and star the whale rallies so they show at the top of the list.
Endgame: stagger waves 1 min apart and relaunch the moment marches return — never let troops sit idle.

groups.heading: Before the event
items: Upgrade the Pitfall to Level 5 with Explosive Arrowheads. That's a +25% attack boost for the entire alliance — the single biggest lever available, and it needs doing during the preparation stage.

Move your city next to the trap. Alliance members should interlock borders tightly with no gaps so troops deploy faster and get more hits in. Mostly a late-game concern — early on, members hopping between alliances makes this messy.
Save preset formations. Rallies fill and launch in seconds; if you're building a march from scratch you've already missed it.
Line up your buffs: pet buff active, Field Commander minister slot registered. Gems can also buy city ATK / Lethality / Deployment Capacity bonuses, though that's really a whale expense.

groups.heading: During the event
items: Archers are the damage. Ratios shift from balanced early to 10/10/80 by Gen 4; late game aim for ~98% archer capacity in every combat march. When joining rather than leading, 20/30/50 is fine.
Star the whale rallies. The star feature pins a player's rally to the top of the list instead of newest-at-the-bottom — a big help if you're slow to react.
Leading: all three of your heroes' skills fire, no matter which one is captain, so position doesn't matter. Pick the best offensive trio for your generation.

Joining: only the top expedition skill counts, and only from the four joiners with the highest skill levels. A wrong hero can displace a good one and drag the whole rally down — send troops with no hero rather than the wrong hero.
Troop levels matter too. Hero skills aren't the whole picture; higher-tier troops and the right ratio move the number just as much.

qa.a: An alliance-wide PvE rally event against the Bear. Everyone piles marches into rallies aimed at the trap, and the damage you deal is what earns you points.
Every two days — a cooldown of two daily in-game resets. Take part today and you're eligible again two days later.
So members in different time zones can each find a slot that suits them. You only get one: if you joined Bear Trap 1 you cannot also join Bear Trap 2 — you wait two days for the next Trap 1.
At the Bear Hunt trap on the alliance's territory. Marches travel there, so the closer your city sits the more hits you land.
Whales and big accounts lead rallies; everyone else fills them. Alliance leadership assigns wave slots before the event so launches stay staggered.
It's one of the highest-value events in the game, it's pure PvE so your troops don't die, and points scale directly with damage — which is why hero choice and troop ratio matter so much.
